It is difficult to define that future as something real in a philosophical sense, but to pretend that it doesn't have some kind of existence seems absurd.

Maybe I'm nice and even have my guys clean up the scrap, and now all you have is a scarred piece of property from the excavation.

This is difficult because we are talking about intentional things here (instead of biological processes), but my point is that our contract for building the home created a reasonable expectation, that barring any natural disaster or abandonment of the project, would reasonably result in a home (the quality of the home is irrelevant). Without my decision to abort that project, my crew would have kept on showing up and building that structure until it was complete.

The interesting part would be that almost any court would find you were owed damages, regardless of the philosophy of what caused the damage. You would sue, and win.

Therefore, not a single one of her somatic or germ cells has the same genetic material as the child, thereby making it definitely not her body. This opens up a whole new can of worms concerning your "ownership" of your own genetic material, but we'll ignore that here.

You can begin to see that these pro-abortion arguments are now making totally arbitrary the point at which we deem life valuable.
